citations.title: Ml Exercise Guide
citations.text:
Assignment 3: Preventing Data Leakage
Task. A student standardizes the whole dataset, then splits it into train and test sets. What is wrong?
Expected answer. The scaler computed the mean and standard deviation using the test rows, so information from the test set leaked into the training pipeline. The correct procedure is to split first, fit the scaler on the training set only and apply the fitted scaler to the test set. Using a scikit-learn Pipeline inside cross-validation automates this.

S2.title: Ml Lecture Notes
S2.text: 1. Supervised and Unsupervised Learning Machine learning builds models that learn patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules. In supervised learning every training example has a label: the model learns a mapping from features X to a target y. Classification predicts a category, such as spam or not spam; regression predicts a continuous number, such as a house price. In unsupervised learning there are no labels and the goal is to discover structure. Clustering, for example k-means, groups similar examples, and dimensionality reduction, for example PCA, compresses features while keeping most of the variance. Semi-supervised learning mixes a small labeled set with a large unlabeled set, and reinforcement learning learns from rewards obtained by acting in an environment. S3.title: Ml Reference Notes
S3.text: Feature: an input variable used by a model, for example a person's age. Label or target: the value the model should predict. Hyperparameter: a setting chosen before training, such as the learning rate, tree depth or number of neighbors k. Parameter: a value learned during training, such as the weights of linear regression. Epoch: one full pass through the training data. Batch size: the number of examples used for one gradient update. Learning rate: the step size of gradient descent. Regularization: a penalty that discourages overly complex models. L2 (ridge) shrinks weights; L1 (lasso) can set weights to zero. Overfitting: low training error but high validation error because the model memorized noise. Underfitting: high error on both training and validation data because the model is too simple. Bias: error from wrong or overly simple assumptions.

S4.title: Ml Lecture Notes
S4.text:
2. Training, Loss and Gradient Descent
Training means choosing model parameters that minimize a loss function measured on the training
data. Mean squared error is a common loss for regression and cross-entropy (log loss) for
classification. Gradient descent iteratively updates parameters in the direction opposite to the
gradient of the loss: w becomes w minus the learning rate times the gradient. If the learning rate is
too large the loss may diverge; if it is too small training is slow.
Stochastic gradient descent computes the gradient on one example and mini-batch gradient descent
on a small batch, which is faster per step and adds helpful noise. One pass through the entire training
set is called an epoch. Linear regression has a closed-form solution, whereas logistic regression,
neural networks and many other models are trained with iterative optimization.

S5.title: Ml Lecture Notes
S5.text: 5. Data Splitting and Cross-Validation Data is usually divided into a training set for fitting, a validation set for tuning hyperparameters and a test set used once for the final unbiased estimate. Using the test set repeatedly for decisions leaks information and makes the estimate optimistic. Data leakage more generally means that information from outside the training data, such as future values or the target itself, influences the features; it produces unrealistically good scores that collapse in production. k-fold cross-validation splits the training data into k equal folds. The model is trained k times, each time holding out a different fold for validation, and the k scores are averaged. Typical values are k = 5 or k = 10. Stratified k-fold preserves the class proportions in every fold and is recommended for classification with imbalanced classes.

S6.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S6.text:
4. Class Imbalance and Validation Practice
For imbalanced classification set class_weight='balanced' so that rare classes receive a larger
weight in the loss, or resample the training folds. Oversampling must be done inside each training
fold only; oversampling before splitting leaks duplicated rows into the validation fold. Report the
precision-recall curve or F1 rather than accuracy.
A common validation setup is StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42). The
helper cross_val_score(estimator, X, y, cv=5, scoring='f1') returns one score per fold. For time
series use TimeSeriesSplit so that the training data always come before the validation data.

S7.title: Ml Exercise Guide
S7.text:
Assignment 1: Diagnosing a Model
Task. You trained a decision tree classifier and obtained 99% training accuracy but 71% validation accuracy. Explain what is happening and propose two fixes.
Expected answer. The large gap between training and validation accuracy is the signature of overfitting (high variance). Fixes include limiting the maximum depth of the tree, requiring a minimum number of samples per leaf, pruning, switching to a random forest, or collecting more data. Report validation performance using cross-validation rather than a single split.

S8.title: Python Exercise Guide
S8.text:
Exercise Set B: Functions and Collections
Exercise B1. Write a function average(numbers) that returns the arithmetic mean of a list. Handle an empty list by returning None instead of dividing by zero.
Exercise B2. Count word frequency. Given a sentence, build a dictionary mapping each lowercase word to its count. Use counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1. Alternative: collections.Counter.
Exercise B3. Remove duplicates from a list while preserving order. Converting to a set removes duplicates but loses ordering; use a seen set and an output list, or dict.fromkeys(items).
Exercise B4. Explain why the following function is buggy: def add_item(item, items=[]): items.append(item); return items. Answer: the default list is created once and shared between calls, so items accumulate across calls. The fix is to use None as the default.

S10.title: Ml Exercise Guide
S10.text:
Assignment 4: Hyperparameter Tuning Plan
Task. Describe how you would tune a random forest.
Expected answer. Define a search space for n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_leaf and max_features. Use stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the training data with grid search or randomized search, select the configuration with the best mean validation score, retrain on all training data, and report the final score once on the held-out test set.
